CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Referral Reason: Prenatal testing at 16 weeks gestation with abnormal ultrasound findings
Clinical Details: Abnormal ultrasound findings detected during routine prenatal screening

TEST PERFORMED
Targeted G-banded chromosome analysis of chromosome 21 and sex chromosomes following rapid PCR of uncultured amniocytes

METHODOLOGY
Amniotic fluid cells were cultured using standard techniques. Metaphase chromosomes were prepared and G-banded according to laboratory protocols. Targeted analysis focused on chromosome 21 and sex chromosomes based on prior rapid PCR results. A minimum of 20 metaphases were examined.

RESULTS
Karyotype: 47,XX,+21

ABNORMAL FEMALE KARYOTYPE
Primary trisomy 21 detected in all cells analyzed
Sex chromosomes: XX (female)
No other structural abnormalities identified in the targeted analysis

INTERPRETATION
This result confirms the presence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in a female fetus. The finding of three copies of chromosome 21 in all cells examined is consistent with primary trisomy 21, which typically results from nondisjunction during meiosis or, less commonly, from a post-zygotic mitotic error. This karyotype finding is consistent with the abnormal ultrasound findings and confirms the previous rapid PCR results.

The recurrence risk for trisomy 21 in future pregnancies is increased above the maternal age-related risk, estimated at approximately 1% plus the age-related risk.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss the implications of this diagnosis
2. Parental karyotyping is not indicated as this appears to be primary trisomy 21
3. For future pregnancies:
   - Combined first trimester screening (biochemical markers and ultrasound)
   - Detailed ultrasound monitoring
   - Prenatal diagnosis (CVS or amniocentesis) is available if desired
4. Referral to appropriate support services and Down syndrome organizations

This analysis was performed in accordance with current professional guidelines and laboratory quality standards.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
